Sea Limited Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results 
 
 
Singapore, November 10, 2026 – Sea Limited (NYSE: SE) (“Sea” or the “Company”) today 
announced its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. 
 
In the third quarter of 2026, Sea’s GAAP revenue was US$8.6 billion, up 43.4% year-on-year. The 
Company also achieved gross profit of US$3.9 billion, up 51.4% year-on-year, and net income of 
US$502.5 million, up 34.0% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA1 increased by 28.9% year-on-year to 
reach US$931.3 million. 
 
“Our strong momentum from the first half of the year has continued into the third quarter. We 
are pleased with this solid performance, and will continue to focus on executing our priorities with 
discipline,” said Forrest Li, Sea’s Chairman and Chief Executive Officer.  
 
On Shopee, he said, “Shopee delivered another strong quarter, again achieving new record highs 
in both top- and bottom-line metrics. Our strategies have proven effective at strengthening our 
fundamentals, giving us a growing buyer base, stronger monetization, and improving unit 
economics.”  
 
On Monee, Mr. Li said, “Monee also delivered another quarter of healthy growth while staying 
disciplined in how we manage risk and how we invest. We are reaching more users, deepening 
relationships with existing ones, and extending credit into more everyday spending scenarios, both 
on- and off-Shopee.”  
 
On Garena, Mr. Li said, “Garena delivered a solid third quarter, with bookings continuing to grow 
and profitability continuing to improve. Free Fire anchored this performance with strong bookings 
growth, and Arena of Valor continued its strong momentum from its 10th year anniversary 
celebrations.” 
 
 
Third Quarter 2026 Business Highlights  
 
▪ Shopee 
o Gross orders totaled 4.5 billion for the quarter, increasing by 25.5% year-on-year. 
o GMV was US$39.7 billion for the quarter, increasing by 23.3% year-on-year. 
o GAAP revenue was US$6.1 billion, up 41.3% year-on-year.  
o GAAP revenue included US$5.3 billion of GAAP marketplace revenue, which 
consists of core marketplace revenue and value-added services revenue and 
increased by 40.9% year-on-year. 
• Core marketplace revenue, mainly consisting of transaction-based fees and 
advertising revenues, was up 50.6% year-on-year to US$4.6 billion. 
• Value-added services revenue, mainly consisting of revenues related to 
logistics services, was US$724.4 million, as compared to US$723.6 million 
for the third quarter of 2025. 

2 
 
o Adjusted EBITDA1 was US$269.2 million, up 44.7% year-on-year. 
 
▪ Monee 
o GAAP revenue was US$1.6 billion, up 63.9% year-on-year. 
o Adjusted EBITDA1 was US$298.3 million, up 15.5% year-on-year. 
o Monee revenue and operating income are primarily attributed to the consumer and 
SME credit business. As of September 30, 2026, consumer and SME loans 
principal outstanding was US$12.6 billion, up 60.0% year-on-year. This consists of 
US$11.2 billion on-book and US$1.3 billion off-book loans principal outstanding2. 
o Non-performing loans past due by more than 90 days as a percentage of consumer 
and SME loans principal outstanding, which includes both on-book and off-book 
loans principal outstanding2, was 1.3%, as compared to 1.1% for the third quarter 
of 2025.  
 
▪ Garena 
o Bookings3 were US$890.0 million, up 5.9% year-on-year. 
o GAAP revenue was US$840.1 million, up 28.6% year-on-year. 
o Adjusted EBITDA1 was US$458.2 million, up 45.9% year-on-year.  
o As mentioned in our prior earnings release, we have excluded the net effect of 
changes in deferred revenue and its related cost in Adjusted EBITDA but continue 
to disclose it as supplemental information. The net effect of changes in deferred 
revenue and its related cost was US$52.0 million, as compared to US$151.9 million 
for the third quarter of 2025. 
o Quarterly active users were 671.7 million, as compared to 670.8 million for the 
third quarter of 2025. 
o Quarterly paying users were 68.6 million, up 4.1% year-on-year. Paying user ratio 
was 10.2%, as compared to 9.8% for the third quarter of 2025.  
o Average bookings per user were US$1.33, as compared to US$1.25 for the third 
quarter of 2025. 
 
Share Repurchase Program  
 
Pursuant to our US$1.0 billion share repurchase program, as of today, we have repurchased 11.1 
million shares for an aggregate amount of US$997.2 million. In addition, on November 9, 2026, 
the board of directors approved an additional US$1.0 billion to the Company’s share repurchase 
authorization, without expiration. 
 
The timing, amount, and method of any share repurchases under the new authorization will be 
determined based on market conditions and other considerations.

Other Operating Income

and 2025, respectively. Other operating income mainly consists of rebates from our logistics 
services providers.

General and Administrative Expenses  
 
Our general and administrative expenses increased by 25.1% to US$425.2 million in the third 
quarter of 2026 from US$340.0 million in the third quarter of 2025.  
 
Provision for Credit Losses  
 
Our provision for credit losses increased by 82.3% to US$681.5 million in the third quarter of 
2026 from US$373.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. 
 
Research and Development Expenses  
 
Our research and development expenses increased by 5.4% to US$301.7 million in the third 
quarter of 2026 from US$286.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. 
 
Non-operating Income or Losses, Net  
 
Non-operating income or losses mainly consist of interest income, interest expense, investment 
gain (loss), foreign exchange gain (loss) and gain (loss) on debt extinguishment. We recorded a net 
non-operating income of US$123.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, as compared to a net non-
operating income of US$61.2 million in the third quarter of 2025. The non-operating income in 
the third quarter of 2026 was primarily due to investment gain of US$65.2 million and interest 
income of US$62.2 million. 
 
Income Tax Expense  
 
We had a net income tax expense of US$280.4 million and US$161.1 million in the third quarter 
of 2026 and 2025, respectively.  
 
Net Income or Loss 
 
As a result of the foregoing, our net income increased by 34.0% to US$502.5 million in the third 
quarter of 2026 from US$375.0 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Diluted earnings per share attributable to Sea Limited’s ordinary shareholders was US$0.78 in the

About Sea Limited 
 
Sea Limited (NYSE: SE) is a global technology company founded in Singapore in 2009. Its mission 
is to better the lives of consumers and small businesses with technology. Sea operates three core 
businesses across e-commerce, digital financial services, and digital entertainment, known as 
Shopee, Monee, and Garena respectively. Shopee is the largest e-commerce platform in Southeast 
Asia and Taiwan and is a leading e-commerce platform in Brazil. Monee is a leading digital financial 
services provider in Southeast Asia with a growing presence in Latin America. Garena is a leading 
global online games developer and publisher.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures 
 
To supplement our consolidated financial statements, which are prepared and presented in 
accordance with U.S. GAAP, we use the following non-GAAP financial measures to help evaluate 
our operating performance: 
 
• “Adjusted EBITDA” for our Shopee segment, Monee segment, Garena segment and Other 
Services segment represents operating income (loss) plus depreciation and amortization 
expenses. We believe that the segment adjusted EBITDA helps to identify underlying trends 
in our operating results, enhancing their understanding of the past performance and future 
prospects. As mentioned in our prior earnings release, we have excluded the net effect of 
changes in deferred revenue and its related cost in Adjusted EBITDA for our Garena segment 
but continue to disclose it as supplemental information. 
 
• “Total adjusted EBITDA” represents the sum of adjusted EBITDA of all our segments 
combined, plus unallocated expenses. We believe that the total adjusted EBITDA helps to 
identify underlying trends in our operating results, enhancing their understanding of the past 
performance and future prospects. 
 
These non-GAAP financial measures have limitations as analytical tools. None of the above 
financial measures should be considered in isolation or construed as an alternative to revenue, net 
loss/income, or any other measure of performance or as an indicator of our operating 
performance. These non-GAAP financial measures presented here may not be comparable to 
similarly titled measures presented by other companies. Other companies may calculate similarly 
titled measures differently, limiting their usefulness as comparative measures to Sea’s data. We 
compensate for these limitations by reconciling the non-GAAP financial measures to their nearest 
U.S. GAAP financial measures, all of which should be considered when evaluating our 
performance. We encourage you to review our financial information in its entirety and not rely on 
any single financial measure.

regularly by monitoring each segment's actual financial and operating performance against 
projections as part of the Company's business planning and budgeting process. Amounts are
